approach.method_basis: The Parent breeds new molecular graphs from its best accepted molecules, using rank-weighted parent selection, connected-fragment crossover and ordinary mutations. It retains an archive of real session-local scores and greedily keeps survivors. A count-fingerprint Gaussian process fits the accepted scores and ranks a fresh offspring pool by correlated sampled functions. After three consecutive non-improving batches, only the forty highest predicted means remain eligible; the first real improvement releases that restriction. Canonical identity checks, the sulfur-introduction gate and bounded valid fallback remain part of this algorithm.
approach.novelty: Replace standardized raw-score targets with exact tie-preserving normal midranks, while retaining the Parent's covariance and sampled exploration. This is an explicit reuse of a historical target variant whose ordering and endpoint predictions failed. The new condition is that the transformed means also determine the stalled top-forty eligible set. The positive affine output wrapper is not a new method. Recent siblings removed residual influence, count multiplicity or crossover, or replaced regression by local probit inference; this Child retains those useful Parent capabilities and tests only the historical target operation on the masked host.

observed_bottleneck: The limiting behavior is that useful exploration does not consistently select or accumulate large real improvements, even though the Parent already has a functioning sampled selector. The actual code Parent and formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de completes all fifteen Search cells with mean 0.607030316211131, population seed SD 0.030175277546149237 and seed macros 0.649701282562401, 0.585233817344553 and 0.586155848726439. Reading its three summary.json and run.log files confirms successful budget-complete results; the historical scheduler warning is retained, not interpreted as a failed run. The read-only Parent audit at policy/scratch/r0062-00-improve-L01/parent-evidence-audit.json, with fifteen individually cited Search logs/trajectories in audit-seed-<seed>-<task>.json, reproduces 435 fits, 88 restricted announcements, 4350 paid outcomes, full gain mass 5.978073077532332 and late mass 1.0224077547621127 over 2175 late purchases. The normal-midrank operation changes standardized targets in all 435 archives; this is opportunity evidence, not benefit. Raw-mean purchased strict-pair accuracy is 13773/19495=0.7064888432931521; it is 2572/3937=0.6532893065786132 on restricted batches and 11201/15558=0.7199511505334876 elsewhere, with no predictive ties in this audit. These selected-stream strata are not controlled comparisons of the mask. Restricted and unrestricted residual-removal siblings n-2d61abf0b2bd and n-7d9afd9af925 lose 0.018621410181405656 and 0.09438631107688404 respectively; preserve their measured residual capability rather than claiming mean-only ranking is adequate. The most direct counterevidence is n-ae12ccae8c7b on n-62daf219c70a: the algebraically identical transform changed all 435 target vectors and purchase sets, but mean batch Spearman was 0.4431662971746234 versus its same-purchased-label raw reference 0.48429892962973947, and matched endpoint delta was -0.021067064526871015. Six endpoints improved and nine declined; all median_2 endpoints improved despite worse ordering, so ranking is not an established mediator. Its implementation was confirmed while its ordering/benefit prediction failed. The specific testable revisit is the new eligibility consumer on the masked Parent, not a claim that the earlier failure was technical or that a monotone transform is inherently better.

adoptions.applicability: The current Parent already fits accepted session-local count-kernel targets. The element supplies the frozen target operation; campaign history establishes its prior failure and the masked consumer supplies the limited revisit condition. No published performance result establishes molecular ranking or endpoint gain here.
adoptions.borrowed_element: Map empirical objective quantiles through the standard-normal inverse CDF before surrogate fitting.

deviations.adopted_setting: One current molecular session only; exact finite midranks without clipping, inherited fixed count GP and correlated selection, original raw affine wrapper explicitly labeled ordinal.
deviations.paper_setting: Cross-task hyperparameter transfer with a learned parametric prior and Winsorized empirical CDF.
deviations.reason: Preserve task isolation and the frozen single target intervention; reuse the existing historical variant and test its new eligibility consumer.

adoptions.implementation_change: In optimize.py normal_midrank_targets and FingerprintPosterior.fit, compute exact tied midranks and standardized normal coordinates from the current accepted archive and use them only in the existing GP solve.

literature_review.conclusion: Reuse only the normal-quantile element in the supplied review. The paper is a construction reference, not permission for repeated tuning or evidence that this historical failed transform will work. Internal evidence provides the specific test: target changes are exposed on the current Parent, useful residual influence is retained, and the new mean-eligibility consumer is measured explicitly. Reject cross-task training, a learned prior, clipping, covariance fitting, new assets and new identities; separate current-host ordering repair from full gain and endpoint attainment.
queries: Reuse frozen search-policy-r62-kernel-mixtures-and-quantile-copulas; direct primary-source reread: https://proceedings.mlr.press/v119/salinas20a/salinas20a.pdf, Section3 and Figure1, on2026-10-22. No additional search-engine query was issued by this role.

sources.applicability: Only the monotone target idea is used, with finite exact midranks from one session. Its identical campaign variant already failed on the old host; current stall-mask applicability is the limited revisit, with no transfer data or new identity.
sources.finding: Objective quantiles can be mapped through the normal inverse CDF for a copula-modeling target; the published approach also learns a cross-task prior.
sources.title: Salinas, Shen and Perrone, A Quantile-based Approach for Hyperparameter Transfer Learning, ICML2020

hypothesis: At each inherited FingerprintPosterior.fit over the complete current accepted archive, keep the original finite raw scores y and their original mean mu_y and scale s_y=max(population_sd(y),0.001). For each record compute L_i=count(y_j<y_i), E_i=count(y_j==y_i), u_i=(L_i+0.5*E_i)/N, z_i=Phi_inverse(u_i), and t_i=(z_i-mean(z))/max(population_sd(z),0.001), retaining archive order and exact ties. Use t only as the right-hand side of the existing Cholesky solve. All-tied archives produce exactly zero targets. There is no clipping, fitted map, score window, hyperparameter search or synthetic label. With the unchanged count-kernel training factor L, active alpha=cholesky_solve(t,L). Return location mu_y+s_y*k_transpose*alpha as an ordinal utility proxy, never expected raw score or an inverse-CDF estimate. Keep every Gram block, observation noise SD0.05, jitter/factor law, normalized conditional covariance, raw amplitude s_y, original normal block, correlated residual, sequential sampled-row maxima and first-index ties. The original mean-ranking consumer now reads that active location, including the inherited K3/M40 stall mask; the stall predicate/reset, parent ranking, archive and survival still read real raw outcomes. The causal prediction is changed target geometry -> changed location rankings and at least one exposed stalled eligibility set -> changed paid identities with real accepted-feedback reuse -> better prospective strict-pair ordering on this masked host. Increased full real gain is a separate performance prediction. The target operation and selection law are the historical variant var-ae12ccae8c7b-000000000005: its latent affine wrapper and this original-raw wrapper yield the same standardized sampled ordering because both have a positive scale. Only the current host's added eligibility consumer supplies the revisit condition; this is not a new likelihood, kernel, residual, mask predicate, model identity or method replacement.

finding_summary.headline: Normal-rank targets changed the stalled masks, but worsened paid ordering and endpoint scores
finding_summary.insights:
The new eligibility consumer was genuinely exercised, so the current-host failure cannot be explained by an unchanged mask, unused transformed predictions or feedback that never reached later fits. The borrowed quantile-to-normal operation worked arithmetically; its restricted single-session adaptation did not improve useful ordering. This settles the registered ordering-repair prediction on the masked Parent while preserving the older experiment’s verdict and leaving the broader approach open. Ordering is not a complete explanation of endpoint utility: the first two median-task seeds improved endpoints despite substantial ordering losses, while two decoration-hopping seeds improved ordering and lost endpoints.

The method found more incumbent improvements—315 versus 253 overall, and 104 versus 76 late—but their mean sizes shrank from 0.023629 to 0.017317 overall and from 0.013453 to 0.004445 late. Fewer stalled announcements, 54 versus 88, therefore did not mean stronger progress. The accepted chemistry audit shows narrower exploration as well: typed/generic scaffold counts fell from 1,667/951 to 1,353/693, and fragment-excluded nearest-prior similarity rose from 0.73554 to 0.77636. Molecules above fifty heavy atoms increased from 44 to 245, while tiny fragments remained. These observations support a limitation in sustained exploration of productive alternative cores and in preserving the magnitude of progress; they do not establish scaffold diversity or size as rewards. A surrogate that retains useful cardinal score gaps, or a proposal/search scheme that preserves alternate core and linker arrangements, could address different parts of that limitation. The present paired test cannot identify which is the mediator. Reactive functionality and unresolved stereochemistry in the generated families are additional representation concerns, not demonstrated causes of the score loss. The negative contribution is specific to this target variant within the retained selector, covariance, mask and graph composition; those components were not separately priced.
finding_summary.results: All fifteen evaluations completed. The transform changed all 435 fitted target vectors and locations, all 54 exposed stalled eligibility sets, and 434 of 435 purchased sets. It bought 2,255 identities absent from the same-state raw-GP selection; 2,167 entered later fits and 684 later generated accepted offspring. On exactly the same 19,305 paid pairs with unequal outcomes, ordering accuracy fell from 68.573% for the raw reference to 66.775% for the active model, a loss of 1.797 percentage points. Mean batch Spearman also fell, from 0.469391 to 0.434704. There were no missing paired predictions; both models had two predictive ties, credited equally. Ordering was worse in 11 of 15 cells and in both restricted and unrestricted batches. The primary ordering falsifier therefore triggered despite verified construction and activation. Separately, mean endpoint score fell from 0.6070303162 to 0.5721583597, a paired change of -0.0348719565; all three seed means fell, with six task-seed gains and nine losses. Full incumbent gain fell from 5.97807308 to 5.45499373 over 4,350 purchases, and late gain from 1.02240775 to 0.46232607 over 2,175 purchases. The registered full-progress prediction and +0.002 endpoint criterion were also not met.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich heteroaromatics and amines, with reactive halogenation, undefined stereochemistry and a large-molecule tail
molecular.overall_character: This assessment covers all 4,350 optimizer proposals and 150 supplied initial records for Child n-8c806cf9b586, and the complete corresponding published Search trajectories of code Parent and formal Anchor n-cf8d309c06de. The frozen comparison reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true for seeds 0/1/2, with no profile mismatch; all fifteen task/seed trajectory pairs exist and their initial molecule/score records match. No task is omitted. Child staging files, rather than a presumed future archive, were the actual inputs. Immutable byte-identical run-local snapshots preserve them. The full input manifest, original staging paths, run-relative snapshot and published Parent file citations, input hashes, descriptor definitions and thirty cell-audit citations are in policy/scratch/r0062-00-improve-L01/molecular/verified/molecular-audit.json. Only that verified audit set supports this report; the earlier scratch audit is superseded because its broad double-bond flag also counted sulfonyl groups and its charge count measured net charge only. Every quoted molecule below is a literal Child trajectory string, with citation order matching the explanations. Parent structures are described from published files without adding them to the Child-only trusted SMILES citation set. Typical output is a neutral, multiply substituted ring system: median 30 heavy atoms, four perceived rings and three aromatic rings. The digest ring-closure rates range from 0.9690 to 0.9897 and aromatic-atom-presence rates from 0.9356 to 0.9885; these are molecule-level text flags, not fractions of atoms. Amides, imides, ethers, heteroaromatic nitrogens, aliphatic amines and carbon-bound halogens are plainly present. Multiply halogenated carbon centres occur in 46 Child proposals and 24 Parent proposals, so neither their total absence nor absence of amines is a supported gap. The output also includes 1,143 molecules with N-halogen bonds, 218 with O-halogen bonds, 85 with acyl halides and 382 with carbon-centred cumulated double bonds; the corresponding Parent counts are 888, 162, 8 and 5. These flags overlap and are structural concerns, not measured instability. There are 106 Child molecules below twelve heavy atoms and 245 above fifty, compared with Parent 124 and 44. The Child spans one to 117 heavy atoms. Across the complete output there are 1,353 distinct nonempty typed and 693 generic Bemis-Murcko scaffolds versus Parent 1,667 and 951; diversity is substantial overall but several high-score families are concentrated. Mean nearest-prior accepted Morgan similarity is 0.7763568409596122 over 4,244 eligible Child proposals versus 0.73553992783322 over 4,226 Parent proposals. Both comparison members must have at least twelve heavy atoms, supplied initial records may be predecessors, and neither future records nor unpurchased alternatives enter this statistic. No Child proposal specifies a tetrahedral configuration; 1,966 contain an unassigned centre. There is one internally charge-separated, net-neutral molecule, rather than a complete absence of charge notation. Synthetic plausibility is questionable because familiar medicinal-chemistry fragments coexist with reactive termini, unusual ring connectivity and undefined configurations. These are graph-based observations, not synthesis, conformer, stability or activity measurements. The report does not identify an objective-required missing pharmacophore beyond the observed associations, attribute chemistry to a component, judge activation or make a selection decision.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals centre on indole-like fused bicyclic cores with aryl or pyridyl carboxamides, methyl groups and ether/thioether substituents. Median size is 25 heavy atoms and three perceived rings; the range is one to 45 heavy atoms. Citations 1 and 2 are seed-0 leaders at evaluations 251 and 103, scores 0.4592143495329135 and 0.4572645941803378: three aromatic rings, a carboxamide, and an allenyl sulfur or oxygen substituent. Citation 1 also has an N-OH substituent. Citations 3 and 4 are the seed-1 and seed-2 maxima at evaluations 285 and 286, both 0.42762099872850584, with N-brominated or N-fluorinated indole-like nitrogens. These are recognizable medicinal skeletons with questionable appendages. The Parent also concentrated on substituted indole carboxamides: its same-seed maxima were 0.42348216717712805, 0.4387992465191 and 0.45050436981567554. Parent and Child have comparable median size, while carbon-centred cumulenes occur in 267 Child proposals versus two Parent proposals.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 352 proposals; allenyl and cyclic cumulated systems are frequent. Small-ring cumulenes and N-halogenated heterocycles warrant a structural feasibility or stability assessment that these trajectories do not supply.
Thirty proposals have fewer than twelve heavy atoms, including late zero-score fragments. Ordinary valence parsing does not make those fragments useful analogues of the connected leaders.
missing_features: The leaders already have aromatic rings, heteroaromatic acceptors and an amide; there is no evidence for a wholly absent target-specific functional group. What is missing from the high-score examples is a demonstrated series that preserves their compact polar/aromatic arrangement while avoiding N-halogen, N-O and cumulene substitutions.

Alternative stable core/linker arrangements are thinly represented around the leaders: the highest 29 proposals in each seed occupy only seven, four and six typed scaffolds. This is limited local coverage, not proof that the generator cannot build another core.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The supplied seed-0 trimethoxy aryl carboxamide, citation 5, scores 0.3051048083696145. The allenyl and pyridyl variants score higher, but this is a multi-edit association rather than an isolated allene effect. The bulky 33-heavy-atom extra-thioamide/aryl variant in citation 6 scores 0.0005383674511498478 at seed 1 evaluation 12; the fragment F in citation 7 scores zero at seed 2 evaluation 292. The visible gradient favours a compact, connected aromatic carboxamide arrangement over fragmentation or elaboration with extra bulky aromatic functionality. Citation 8, the seed-2 final molecule, retains the ring-amide family but carries a cyclic cumulene and N-Cl and scores 0.4067656765249372. This trajectory does not show that additional rings, more halogen or more aromatic bulk would universally help.

per_task.generated_character: This is the largest and most aromatic output family: median 44 heavy atoms, five perceived rings and five aromatic rings across 870 proposals. There are 231 proposals above fifty heavy atoms, compared with 18 in the Parent. Citations 1 and 2 are seed-1 evaluations 274 and 281, both scoring 0.6251349163518618: dense six-ring aza/oxa aromatic assemblies bearing cyanate esters, a sulfur-containing side chain and carbonyl halides. They differ by oxygen versus sulfur attachment at one carbonyl-chloride substituent. Citation 3 is the seed-0 maximum at evaluation 290, score 0.6109936575052854, containing imide carbonyls, an imine-linked chain and unusually large aza-aromatic rings. Citation 4 is the seed-2 maximum at evaluation 283, score 0.6131221719457014: a substituted aryl/imide assembly with a carbonate, thiocarbonyl and cumulated linker. The Parent same-seed maxima are 0.8561477222467935, 0.6217289889933668 and 0.6442339647723496. Its seed-0 leader is a smaller 30-heavy-atom fused heterocycle with an O-F group and a thione; the Parent is therefore not a clean synthetic-plausibility reference either.
liabilities: Eighty-three proposals contain acyl halides and 226 contain cyanate esters; among the seed-1 highest twenty-nine, the counts are 27 and 29. These potentially reactive functionalities complicate interpreting high scores as useful compound chemistry.

The long heavy-atom tail, very large aromatic constructions and unusual aza-ring connectivity raise route and conformational feasibility questions. No synthesis or three-dimensional feasibility evidence is available.
missing_features: The current high-score family does not demonstrate stable peripheral substitutions that retain the successful connected core without cyanate esters or carbonyl halides. Their absence from this comparison is a coverage gap, not a proven objective requirement.
Compact alternative scaffold/connectivity arrangements are underexplored in the present seed-1 leader family; unrestricted graph growth has not provided a general substitute for those alternatives.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: An isolated ethane proposal, citation 5 at seed 1 evaluation 213, receives 0.5, while the connected heteroaromatic assemblies score above that floor. Size alone is insufficient: the 117-heavy-atom, 19-ring seed-0 proposal at evaluation 75 scores 0.5674398313095325, below its 41-heavy-atom seed maximum. All twenty-nine highest proposals in seed 1 share one typed and one generic scaffold; citations 1 and 2 tie exactly despite their oxygen/sulfur substitution. The gradient supports some core/connectivity arrangements but gives no evidence that cyanate groups or acyl-halide reactivity are necessary. The substantially different published Parent seed-0 assembly also argues against reading the present large-molecule family as the only useful chemistry.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals have median 32 heavy atoms and three perceived rings. The strongest examples combine aromatic hydrophobic regions with non-amide aliphatic amines, but their connectivity differs substantially between seeds. Citation 1, seed 0 evaluation 275 at 0.9964632593954522, is a flexible biphenyl-containing diamine with a methoxy group, aryl fluorine and an N-bromo substituent. Citation 2, seed 1 evaluation 285 at 0.9999898368637014, combines two aryl rings, a phenol, an imine, a geminal diamine/aminal and an N-ethyl pyrrolidine. Citation 3, seed 2 evaluation 282 at 0.9999978756497574, has 31 heavy atoms and seven perceived rings, a polycyclic tertiary-amine framework, a phenol and an aryl Cl/Br pattern. Free amines and ring nitrogens are therefore present; the output is not missing a basic-centre vocabulary. The Parent has related aryl/amine families with same-seed maxima 0.980206046238846, 0.9999921067161532 and 0.9735180254338864.
liabilities: N-halogen and O-halogen bonds occur in 184 and 167 proposals. Imine/aminal connectivity in a leader and the crowded polycyclic amine framework in another make stability, configuration and accessible conformations unresolved.
Thirteen proposals are below twelve heavy atoms and ten exceed fifty. Neither tail is supported as a universal requirement by the mid-sized leaders.
missing_features: The missing coverage is stereochemically explicit and chemically stable versions of the already-present aryl/amine architectures. There are 851 proposals with unassigned stereocentres and none with a specified configuration.

No net-charged molecular form is represented in these trajectories despite the amine-rich leaders. This is a representation gap; the trajectories do not establish how the scoring pipeline treats protonation or whether another state would improve the score.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Citation 4, seed 2 evaluation 20 at 0.00016650955053713697, is a smaller N-sulfonyl pyrrolidine carboxamide with N-Cl and no comparable freely basic aliphatic nitrogen. Citation 5, seed 0 evaluation 25 at 0.007693720580637529, has 31 heavy atoms but predominantly acid, amide and sulfonamide polar groups. The contrast with the similarly sized amine-rich leaders suggests nitrogen environment and aromatic/amine arrangement matter, rather than size or ring count alone. Citation 6 replaces the aryl chlorine of citation 3 with fluorine and ties it exactly at 0.9999978756497574. These near-ceiling recorded scores do not demonstrate physical binding, nor identify a particular missing group.

per_task.generated_character: The 870 proposals are aromatic nitrogen/carbonyl assemblies with median 32 heavy atoms, four perceived rings and three aromatic rings. Typical motifs are fused aza-arenes, N-N heterocycles, cyclic amides or imides, alkyl substituents and ethers. Citation 1, seed 1 evaluation 281 at 0.2387161398517853, has 35 heavy atoms, an extended fused aromatic region and a large carbonyl-containing N/O ring. Citation 2, seed 0 evaluation 291 at 0.23559321469900382, links an alkoxy aza-arene to an N-N fused heterocycle and a carbonyl-rich saturated ring. Citation 3, seed 2 evaluation 282 at 0.22800192351525037, is a related aza-aromatic assembly with a large hydrazine-containing carbonyl ring. The Parent same-seed maxima are 0.2228098910506594, 0.22127859918153825 and 0.24240057874100313, with related aza-arene/carbonyl chemistry but different bridges and ring saturation. Child nonempty typed/generic scaffold counts are 359/200 versus Parent 559/379, and fragment-excluded mean nearest-prior similarity is 0.776175592235847 versus 0.6874443467646326.
liabilities: There are 268 molecules with a single N-N bond, including non-aromatic hydrazine-like connectivity in the late family. This is a structural flag, not proof that every N-N heterocycle is unstable.

Oversized fused or medium/large heterocycles can be difficult to construct, although ordinary ethers, amides and aza-arenes make parts of these molecules plausible. No route or conformer assessment is supplied.
missing_features: The observed gap is continued coverage of distinct ring/linker arrangements around the useful carbonyl and amine motifs. Carbonyls, heteroaromatic nitrogens and cyclic amines themselves are already present; the score history does not reveal an unseen mandatory group.

Large N/O and N-N rings are represented as two-dimensional connectivity without demonstrated ring-closing routes, conformations or assigned configuration. Chemically resolved alternatives retaining the same polar-group placement remain untested.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Citation 4, the supplied seed-0 aromatic imide ester, scores 0.1678386594791329. Citation 5, a seed-2 evaluation-12 open, amide-substituted aryl/pyrrole derivative, scores 0.12375810255351721. The higher values occur with more integrated cyclic carbonyl/amine connectivity and alkoxy/alkyl aza-aromatic substitution; merely adding aromatic rings does not explain the separation. Citation 6 is the zero-score single-carbon proposal at seed 2 evaluation 278. Citation 7 is the only charge-separated proposal across the Child panel: an N+/N- unit at seed 0 evaluation 285, score 0.2149896558044248. It does not establish a missing charged pharmacophore. The Parent seed-2 leader exceeds the Child seed-2 leader with a different, more saturated bridged carbonyl/N framework, so one fused-aromatic family is not an exclusive local solution.

per_task.generated_character: Across 870 proposals the median is 27 heavy atoms and four perceived rings. The main family comprises carbonyl-rich fused N-heterocycles attached to an aryl/aza-aryl region and a small unsaturated carbocycle, with extensive fluorination and frequent N-halogenation. Citation 1, seed 1 evaluation 243 at 0.6148839606227952, has 29 heavy atoms: an imide-like fused core, a fluorinated cyclobutene, an amino-fluorophenyl substituent, N-N(F)C connectivity and an N-S substituent. Citation 2, seed 0 evaluation 298 at 0.60503466519286, is a 27-heavy-atom non-aromatic four-ring enamine/imine-carbonyl framework with a fluorinated cyclopentene and N-F. Citation 3, seed 2 evaluation 242 at 0.4999874276266219, retains the aromatic carbonyl core and a fluorinated cyclopentene. The Parent same-seed maxima are 0.7658605860985803, 0.6443701453126088 and 0.6201223048692813; their carbonyl/imino, partly saturated N-heterocyclic structures differ in ring and heteroatom placement. They also carry unusual halogenated or strained features, so their larger scores are not a clean chemical-quality standard.
liabilities: N-halogen bonds occur in 532 proposals; all twenty-nine highest proposals of seed 0, twenty-three of seed 1 and twenty-eight of seed 2 contain one. Small unsaturated rings and N-N/N-S attachments add feasibility questions without proving impossibility.

There are 590 proposals with unassigned stereocentres and none with specified configuration, thirty-six proposals below twelve heavy atoms and one above fifty. The nominal high scores do not establish stereochemical identity or synthetic accessibility.
missing_features: Broader ring saturation and carbonyl/imino/amine placement within the compact size regime remain a meaningful coverage gap; the Parent demonstrates alternatives, but no single missing objective-specific pharmacophore can be established from these confounded structures.

The high-score family lacks specified stereochemistry and a demonstrated series free of N-halogen or other unusual N-heteroatom substituents. Ordinary carbon-bound fluorination is available, including multiply halogenated carbons, so fluorine introduction is not absent.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: Both undergrown and overgrown structures score poorly: citation 4 is a 1.1226968762665698e-28 duplicate-core elaboration at seed 2 evaluation 33, and citation 5 is an isolated F proposal at seed 0 evaluation 218 with 1.1043196211273875e-26. But size is insufficient: citation 6 has 27 heavy atoms, a ring-rich fluorinated N-heterocyclic framework and score 3.05792057625101e-09 at seed 0 evaluation 114. The visible preference is for particular local atom, bond and substitution arrangements in a compact multiring scaffold, not simply fluorine count, aromaticity or heavy-atom count. Citation 7, the seed-2 final proposal, scores 0.023953018495137153 despite retaining much of the same carbonyl/halogenated framework. The comparisons do not isolate the contribution of any single functional group.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Source: n-8c806cf9b586 versus its code Parent n-cf8d309c06de, frozen Search seeds 0/1/2, 4,350 optimizer proposals per node, ten supplied initial records plus 290 proposals per cell. N-halogen counts are 1,143 versus 888, O-halogen 218 versus 162, carbonyl-halide 85 versus 8 and carbon-centred cumulene 382 versus 5. One high-score family has carbonyl halides in 27 of its highest 29 molecules and cyanate esters in all 29. These are overlapping structural observations; no stability assay or causal attribution is available.
transferable_gaps.gap: Useful ring and polar-group assemblies are repeatedly decorated with reactive heteroatom bonds rather than explored through a well-resolved stable analogue series.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could distinguish carbon substitution from heteroatom halogenation and expose stable alternatives for reactive local environments while retaining ring and polar-group placement. Its own accepted feedback must decide their usefulness; the present chemistry does not justify a universal reward, forbidden-group filter or claim that these groups caused the score outcome.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Under the same complete Child Search panel, 1,966 of 4,350 proposed molecules have an RDKit-perceived unassigned stereocentre and none has a specified tetrahedral configuration. Only one proposal contains formally charged atoms, an internally charge-separated N+/N- structure with zero net charge; all other proposals lack charge notation. Free aliphatic amines are present among the leaders. Parent proposals also lack specified configurations and explicit charged atoms.
transferable_gaps.gap: Stereogenic output is left configurationally unresolved, and explicit ionisation-state coverage is almost absent.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Where permitted by the molecular representation contract, make configuration and molecular charge state expressible and auditable for graph edits that introduce stereocentres or ionisable groups. Evaluate any benefit from session-local real feedback; neither a universally preferred charge state nor a stereochemical score benefit has been established here.

transferable_gaps.evidence: For this Child under the frozen Search conditions, 1,353 typed and 693 generic nonempty scaffolds occur, versus Parent 1,667 and 951. Nearest-prior accepted Morgan similarity after excluding either member below twelve heavy atoms averages 0.7763568409596122 over 4,244 Child proposals versus 0.73553992783322 over 4,226 Parent proposals. One session has only one typed and one generic scaffold among its highest 29 proposals. These pooled and selected-stratum associations do not show an absolute inability to change scaffold or attribute concentration to a particular component.
transferable_gaps.gap: The output covers many skeletons overall but narrows to closely related high-score families without reliably maintaining alternative core/connectivity options.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose scaffold, linker and ring-connectivity alternatives that preserve useful local chemistry, and use accepted feedback to test whether distinct families remain productive. The evidence motivates coverage diagnostics and a testable capability change, not an assumed universal novelty reward or a claim that more scaffold diversity must improve scores.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The Child produces 106 molecules below twelve heavy atoms and 245 above fifty, compared with Parent 124 and 44. Single atoms and diatomics appear even late. A 117-heavy-atom assembly scores 0.5674398313095325 while its same-session 41-heavy-atom leader scores 0.6109936575052854; elsewhere small connected multiring molecules are useful. These are current-panel output associations, not size laws.
transferable_gaps.gap: Generation still reaches both tiny disconnected-from-leader chemical fragments and excessively expanded assemblies without reliably preserving a productive structural scale.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Make expansion, contraction and fragment reassembly preserve or deliberately reconstruct connected functional arrangements, and track both size tails against session-local outcomes. No single hard minimum, maximum, ring requirement or universal optimum size follows from these molecules.

transferable_gaps.evidence: The Child has sixteen molecules with a perceived ring of four or fewer atoms whose atoms are all aromatic, versus 170 in the Parent. Some leaders instead contain heavily fused or bridged amine frameworks, large N/O rings, cyclic cumulenes or small unsaturated carbocycles. The reduction in one topology flag does not establish feasibility of the remaining structures, and no route or conformer records were provided.
transferable_gaps.gap: Ring-rich output lacks demonstrated geometric and synthetic feasibility despite producing familiar medicinal fragments.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic graph generator could represent ring geometry and feasible local ring transformations more explicitly, while retaining legitimate saturated, fused and bridged chemistry. Treat such checks as hypotheses to evaluate within the authorized contract; graph perception alone neither proves synthesis nor assigns the observed chemistry to the intervention.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
